title: Code spans change after unsuccessful link/image lookahead
prompt:
Parsing an unfinished link or image label can change how later inline code is rendered. For example, '[foo `bar` baz`' should render as '

[foo bar baz`

\n', and the corresponding unfinished image case should preserve its code span too. Also keep a code span from consuming a closing marker beyond the current label boundary: '[`](``)' should remain a link whose visible label is a literal backtick. Correct these inconsistent inline results while preserving normal code spans, link precedence, different backtick-run lengths and ordinary Markdown behavior. Add regression tests.

hardness_evidence.criterion: at least 40 meaningful changed production lines in a stateful algorithm with at least three edge-case families
families: unsuccessful link/image lookahead must not change subsequent tokenization
narrowed label ranges and runs crossing their endpoint
code-span/link precedence with heterogeneous backtick run lengths

setup.build: Native Node TypeScript stripping; tests and hidden runner import src directly, no dist build
setup.baseline_scope: Original upstream test:markdown-it script (functional and pathological tests), excluding packaging/lint/CommonMark standalone suite
setup.deps: Exact minimal runtime/test dependency lock; original source/package manifest unchanged
setup.solver_export: Only buggy source snapshot and prepared node_modules; no Git upstream history, oracle, task metadata or held-out assertions

hidden_test_counts.note: Checks stop at first failing assertion; total denotes registered held-out assertions, not observed partial score.
